text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds tested the top-side of their recent range, slavishly following Treasuries higher late in a day, lacking any meaningful domestic news. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.27, up 0.05 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts closed little changed, failing to hold on to early gains after official UK manufacturing data suggested growth was not strong enough to prompt a pre-election interest rate rise. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-06/32, up 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures climbed for the third successive day as favourable signals from other bond markets, a techncially driven futures session and further talk of buying at the long end of the curve. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.60, up 0.3 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bonds and Btp futures ended firmer on a burst of late short-covering amid market relief a domestic government crisis seemed to have been averted with a compromise with the opposition over an Albanian mission. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.67, up 0.63 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were unchanged at midday, having erased early gains. Treasuries rose in early trade, aided by the dollar's strength overnight. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-15/32, up 02/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.1 percent.

JAPAN - The key June Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on short-covering by dealers toward the close. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 127.05, up 0.20 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The Eurobond market saw steady issuance, with the dollar sector still the main focus. Sigma Finance Corp set a $400 million five-year bond at 18 b.p. over Treasuries. Deals were also launched by LVMH and Credit Local. In French francs, Japan-guaranteed JFM launched its debut in the sector, a 1.0 billion franc 10-year bond. Bankers said JFM was eyeing a parallel bond issue.
